<details><summary>AI design/defect review</summary>

- D1: In `focus update steps`, step 2 fires synchronous `change` and `blur` events before step 4.1 resolves `entry`'s `DOM anchor`'s `node document`. If a `blur` listener adopts the focus target into a same-origin `<iframe>` that has an ongoing intercepted `navigate` event, step 4.1 resolves `document` to the `<iframe>`'s `Document`, designates the adopted element as its focused area, and sets its `focus changed during ongoing navigation` to true, suppressing the `<iframe>`'s post-transition focus reset (whereas Chromium and Gecko leave the `<iframe>` unfocused and still reset its focus). 
- D2: There are currently no WPT tests covering cross-frame `focus changed during ongoing navigation` behavior when an `<iframe>` or its parent intercepts `navigate`. 
- Q1: Which `Document`(s) should have `focus changed during ongoing navigation` set to true when focus moves into, within, or out of a child `<iframe>`?
1. Option a (keep as is): Set it for each `focusable area` `entry` in `new chain` whose `document`'s focused area is not `entry`. Minimal diff, but diverges from Chromium and Gecko when re-entering an `<iframe>`'s previously focused element from the parent (because HTML keeps the `<iframe>`'s `focused area` when focus moves to the parent) and, once #11873 includes the `<iframe>` in `new chain`, when moving focus from a navigating parent into a child `<iframe>`.
2. Option b ([spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q1-b), [tests](https://github.com/noamr/wpt/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q1-b)): Designate `entry` for each `focusable area` in `new chain`, and set `focus changed during ongoing navigation` on `new focus target`'s `Document` when `entry` is `new focus target` and either `document`'s focused area is not `entry` or `old chain` is non-empty. Matches Chromium and Gecko across all cross-frame cases, though a completing parent or child navigation with `[autofocus]` can still pull focus across frames.
3. Option c ([spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q1-c), [tests](https://github.com/noamr/wpt/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q1-c)): Set `focus changed during ongoing navigation` on the `Document`s (and `ancestor navigables`' active documents) of unfocused entries in `old chain` and focused entries in `new chain`. Prevents parent and child SPA transitions from overriding cross-frame focus changes, but changes behavior that Chromium and Gecko currently agree on.
</details>

@noamr Thanks for looking into this. I’m leaning toward option B given the Chromium and Gecko behavior you described. The linked branches return 404 for me. Could you share working links to the spec diff and WPTs for option B? If the D1 case is separate, could you also share a minimal repro for it?

Thanks, @noamr! I applied option B and D1. In headless runs, the WPTs passed 8/8 in Chromium and 5/8 in Firefox 153. Could you take another look at the Firefox results? https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65298

Thanks, @noamr! I split the WPTs into refocus, reset, and destination checks. All four reset controls pass in Chromium and Firefox. The remaining Firefox failures are in the separate refocus and autofocus destination checks. https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65298

Open: Q2.

New in this review:

- Q2: In the focus update steps, the "or `old chain` is not empty" clause from option b only has an effect when the top-level traversable doesn't have system focus. With system focus, the focusing steps return early if `new focus target` is already the currently focused area, so that condition is always true. Without system focus, `old chain` is empty, which gives a different result for the same focus move. Case, in a background window: `childButton` is the `<iframe>` document's focused area and `parentButton` is the parent's. The child has an intercepted `after-transition` navigation, and script calls `childButton.focus()`. The parent's focused area moves from `parentButton` to the `<iframe>`, but because `childButton` already is the child's focused area and `old chain` is empty, the flag isn't set and the child's focus reset still runs. In a focused window, the same calls suppress it. (The clause also relies on reading "current focus chain" as empty when nothing has system focus; that definition says "if *traversable* is non-null", which looks like an older typo for "if the currently focused area is non-null".) Which behavior do we want without system focus?
  1. Option a (keep as is): re-entering the `<iframe>` from the parent doesn't count as a focus change without system focus. Defensible, since nothing "gains focus" then, but it differs from the same calls in a focused window.
  2. Option b ([spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/84fc9a2), [branch](https://github.com/noamr/html/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q2-b)): count a changed path. Before the blur events, note whether any navigable container in `new chain` wasn't already its document's focused area, and set the flag when `entry` is `new focus target` and either `document`'s focused area isn't `entry` or the path changed. Same as today with system focus. Without system focus, re-entering counts and `focus()` on an already focused element doesn't.
  3. Option c ([spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/1cad229), [branch](https://github.com/noamr/html/tree/spec-review/html-13268/q2-c)): drop the condition and always set the flag when `entry` is `new focus target`. Simplest, but without system focus `focus()` on an already focused element would suppress a pending reset, while with system focus the early return prevents that.

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Firefox 160, with the test window behind a second window: calling `focus()` again on the child's already focused button doesn't suppress the child's reset, which matches a and b but not c. For re-entering from the parent, Firefox doesn't move the parent's `activeElement` to the `<iframe>` at all without system focus, so it can't tell a from b. I couldn't add a wpt test for this: opening a popup to take system focus away breaks the harness under `./wpt run` in both Firefox and Chrome.
  </details>

<details><summary>Existing items (Q1, D1, D2)</summary>

- Q1 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968), [JinDX](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6919288876)): Option b, fixed in f29ff97.
- D1 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968)): Fixed in 46e1421. The snapshot also covers the focus target being adopted during the `focus` events fired while walking `new chain`, not just during `blur`.
- D2 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968)): Covered by web-platform-tests/wpt#65298.
- Firefox results ([JinDX](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6934732327), [JinDX](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6935406920)): Under `./wpt run`, all 13 subtests in web-platform-tests/wpt#65298 pass in Firefox 160 locally and in Firefox Nightly in wpt CI. I could reproduce the two refocus failures only when the test window doesn't have system focus, which headless runs outside wptrunner often don't. I couldn't reproduce the two autofocus destination failures. Maybe the refocus subtests could check `document.hasFocus()` first, like the adopt-in-blur test does after `test_driver.click()`? Safari Technology Preview in wpt CI fails the four subtests where the child's `after-transition` reset should move focus from the parent into the `<iframe>`.
</details>

<details><summary>Reviewed commits</summary>

Reviewed at 46e1421 on 985d443, with web-platform-tests/wpt#65298 at d6fc3b3, using spec-pr-review.
</details>

Thanks for checking this, @noamr. I favor option B for Q2. Re-entering the iframe changes the focus path even if the child’s focused element is unchanged. Calling `focus()` again on the same path should leave a pending reset in place.

Does `84fc9a2` depend on #11873 for the iframe container to appear in `new chain`? If so, could we check the ancestor navigables’ containers directly?

I added a click and a `document.hasFocus()` assertion to both refocus tests in web-platform-tests/wpt#65298. All 13 subtests passed locally with `./wpt run` in Firefox Nightly 162. Both refocus tests also passed in Safari Technology Preview CI, which still reports the four `after-transition` reset failures.

Agreed on option B, and good catch on 84fc9a2 — `focus chain` currently stops at `node navigable`'s `parent` (#11886 / #11873), so the `<iframe>` never appears in `new chain`.

Checking the containers directly before firing `blur` sounds much better, and also avoids depending on whether #11873 keeps navigable containers in `new chain`. One small gotcha: start from `new focus target`'s document's own `node navigable` (i.e. `inclusive ancestor navigables` rather than `ancestor navigables`, when `new focus target` is a focusable area with a non-null `node navigable`), since a child `<iframe>` is its own document's `node navigable`'s `container`. (Until #11886 is fixed, the spec also never designates the `<iframe>` as the parent's focused area, though engines already do.)

The `hasFocus()` update in web-platform-tests/wpt#65298 looks good! Might also be worth adding one subtest calling `childButton.focus()` again while already focused on that path during an `after-transition` navigation, to check that the reset still runs.

Thanks, @noamr! df5d2e6 checks the containers before `blur`, including the one for the new focus target’s own document. The new subtest in web-platform-tests/wpt#65298 verifies that calling `childButton.focus()` again still lets the `after-transition` reset run.

Thanks, JinDX — df5d2e6 looks right for Q2. I also opened JinDX/html#1 with a few editorial markup fixes (no normative change), in case you want to merge it into this branch.

<details><summary>Existing items (Q1, Q2, D1, D2)</summary>

- Q1 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968), [JinDX](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6919288876)): Option b, fixed in f29ff97.
- Q2 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6953674378), [JinDX](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6964275674), [noamr](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6977413699)): Option b, fixed in df5d2e6. Until #11886 is fixed, the parent's focused area is never the `<iframe>` in the spec, so for targets inside an `<iframe>` the path always counts as changed.
- D1 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968)): Fixed in 46e1421.
- D2 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13268#issuecomment-6913988968)): Covered by web-platform-tests/wpt#65298.
</details>
